saints.name: St. Teresa of Calcutta
saints.title: Religious and Foundress
saints.shortBlurb: The little Albanian sister who left the classroom for the slums of Calcutta and made the dying poor her whole life…
biography: Born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu at Skopje on 26 August 1910, of Albanian stock, she joined the Sisters of Loreto in Ireland at eighteen and was sent to India in 1929, taking her name from Thérèse of Lisieux. For nearly twenty years she taught at the Loreto school in Entally, Calcutta.

On 10 September 1946, on the train to Darjeeling, she received what she called a 'call within a call' — to leave the convent and serve the poorest of the poor while living among them. In 1948 she put on the white blue-bordered sari and went into the slums; in 1950 her Missionaries of Charity were approved.

The congregation added to the usual vows a fourth: wholehearted free service to the poorest of the poor. In 1952 she opened the Kalighat Home for the Dying, that the abandoned might die with dignity; the work spread worldwide, and in 1979 she received the Nobel Peace Prize.

She died at Calcutta on 5 September 1997 and was given a state funeral by India. Her letters revealed some fifty years of interior darkness borne in faith. Beatified by John Paul II in 2003, she was canonized by Pope Francis on 4 September 2016.
saints.knownFor: Serving Christ in the poorest of the poor through the Missionaries of Charity.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Teresa of Calcutta (vatican.va)
